Cosmic Echo is an interactive astronomical exploration and change-detection platform designed to help users investigate how the infrared universe evolves over time. Using real observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission, accessed through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA), the platform enables users to explore regions of the sky, retrieve astronomical observations, inspect scientific image data, and compare observations taken at different times.

details:
COSMIC ECHO — The Infrared Universe, in Motion

1. What does the project do?

Cosmic Echo is an interactive astronomical exploration and change-detection platform that helps users investigate how the infrared sky changes over time. It is designed around real observations from NASA's SPHEREx mission, accessed through the NASA/IPAC Infrared Science Archive (IRSA).

The application provides a guided scientific workflow through which users can select a region of the sky using Right Ascension (RA) and Declination (Dec), search for available SPHEREx observations, inspect astronomical image data, and investigate differences between observations.

Its central feature, the Cosmic Echo Detector, focuses on comparing observations from different times to identify candidate changes in astronomical sources. Rather than simply subtracting two images, the scientific workflow considers observation compatibility, wavelength information, spatial alignment, image quality, and measurement uncertainty.

2. How does it work?

The platform follows a structured exploration and analysis process:

  • Sky Exploration: Users enter celestial coordinates and a search radius to discover available SPHEREx observations.
  • Data Retrieval: The application accesses astronomical observation records and associated data products through NASA/IPAC IRSA.
  • Observation Inspection: FITS astronomical files are inspected to retrieve science images, image headers, spatial coordinates, wavelength information, and available auxiliary data.
  • Scientific Comparison: Selected observations are assessed for compatibility before comparison. Relevant processing includes spatial alignment, image preparation, difference calculation, and uncertainty analysis where supported by the available data.
  • Candidate Detection: Potentially significant residual differences can be investigated using quality-aware thresholds and image-processing techniques.
  • Results and Reporting: Observation metadata, analysis information, candidate measurements, and scientific limitations can be presented in structured reports.

3. Benefits and Intended Impact

Cosmic Echo aims to make infrared astronomical data more accessible and understandable to students, astronomy enthusiasts, citizen scientists, and researchers.

Its intended benefits include:

  • Making public NASA astronomical observations easier to explore.
  • Providing an accessible introduction to infrared astronomy and scientific image analysis.
  • Helping users investigate potential changes in astronomical sources across observations.
  • Encouraging scientific curiosity and independent investigation.
  • Demonstrating how publicly available space-mission data can be transformed into interactive research experiences.

The broader vision is to bridge the gap between complex astronomical datasets and people who want to understand the dynamic nature of our universe.

4. Tools and Technologies Used

The project was developed using Google Antigravity as an AI-assisted development environment, supporting the development and organization of the application.

The scientific and software technology stack includes:

  • Python: Core programming language for scientific computation and data processing.
  • Streamlit: Interactive application interface.
  • Astropy: Astronomical coordinates, FITS file handling, units, and World Coordinate System (WCS) operations.
  • Astroquery: Access to astronomical archives and NASA/IPAC IRSA services.
  • NumPy: Numerical computation and image-array operations.
  • SciPy: Scientific image processing and numerical analysis.
  • Pandas: Observation metadata management.
  • Matplotlib and Plotly: Scientific image visualization and interactive charts.
  • NASA SPHEREx / IRSA: Primary astronomical data source.

The project is software-based and does not require custom physical hardware.

5. What makes the project creative and innovative?

The central creative idea behind Cosmic Echo is to treat astronomical observations as more than static pictures of space.

Instead of simply displaying astronomical images, the platform focuses on investigating how observations may differ over time. It combines astronomical data discovery, image inspection, scientific comparison, and candidate identification into a single exploration experience.

The Cosmic Echo Detector is the project's defining concept: it transforms the process of comparing astronomical observations into an understandable and interactive workflow.

Another important aspect is its emphasis on scientific responsibility. An image difference is not automatically an astronomical discovery. The platform is designed to consider instrumental artifacts, wavelength incompatibility, spatial misalignment, and uncertainty before interpreting potential changes.

6. Factors Considered During Development

Several important considerations guided the project's design:

  • Scientific accuracy: Use authentic astronomical observations and avoid fabricated measurements or detections.
  • Data compatibility: Account for wavelength coverage, spatial coordinates, image units, resolution, and observation quality before comparing images.
  • Uncertainty: Avoid unsupported statistical significance claims when reliable variance information is unavailable.
  • Accessibility: Make complex astronomical concepts understandable to users without an advanced astronomy background.
  • Performance: Consider large FITS files, archive response times, caching, and processing requirements.
  • Reliability: Handle missing metadata, unavailable observations, incompatible products, and network errors gracefully.
  • Transparency: Clearly distinguish candidate differences from confirmed astronomical discoveries.
  • Maintainability: Use a modular, Python-based architecture that can be extended with additional scientific analysis capabilities.

7. Long-Term Vision

Cosmic Echo aims to grow into an accessible platform for exploring the changing infrared universe. Future improvements could include expanded observation comparisons, more advanced source detection, improved uncertainty modelling, richer scientific reporting, and additional astronomical archive integrations.

Ultimately, the project seeks to make the exploration of our dynamic universe more accessible by turning publicly available space-science observations into opportunities for discovery, learning, and scientific investigation.
